lines.trans: Did you find the three wooden chairs behind the boiler room, Tariq?
I found the chairs, and behind an old stone wall I found this box.
A small cedar wood box? Never in my life have I seen it in fifteen years!

words.gram: singular noun + 1st sg possessive, with ب- (in)

lines.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate on top... wait, read that number!
Let me pull my glasses down off my forehead... Room Nine?!
Tariq, look at the wooden key board behind us: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight!
Our guesthouse all its life has had only eight rooms! Where could Room Nine be?!
Listen when I tilt the box, a piece of metal just slid inside.

words.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

lines.trans: There is a small keyhole on the front, and look what is taped underneath: an old brass key!

words.gloss: there is; there are; is there?

lines.trans: A ninth brass key?! Do we open it tonight or wait until morning?!

lines.trans: Look at the folded map by the hinge, there is a hidden door drawn on this floor!

meanings.note: The number four, used with masculine nouns.

examples.trans: Room four is arriving today.
Four tables and eight chairs in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday word for rice. Often pronounced 'ruz' in Jordanian.

examples.trans: This is an old cedar wood box.
The scent of cedar wood is very pleasant.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أسابيع.

examples.trans: Next week I have time off.
We stayed at the guesthouse all week.

meanings.note: Appears in everyday speech inside warm set phrases such as إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again!').

examples.trans: See you soon, sir!
Goodbye and until next time.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian pronoun 'you' when addressing two or more people.

examples.trans: You are very kind people.
Hold the torch, both of you.

meanings.note: Command to a male to wait.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, I have an idea!
The suitcase is still waiting for its owner.

meanings.note: Attached prefix ب- before nouns ('in/with'); with pronoun suffixes in Levantine it takes the stem في-: فيي ('in me'), فيك ('in/to you m.'), فيكي ('in/to you f.'), فيه ('in him/it'), فيها ('in her/it'), فينا ('in us'), فيهم ('in them').

examples.trans: Welcome to Jasmine House!
My suitcase has a red ribbon in it.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: بواب.

examples.trans: The wooden door is open now.
Someone knocked on the door.

meanings.note: Extremely common Jordanian word meaning both 'only / just' (بس نص كاسة 'just half a glass') and 'but' between clauses.

examples.text: بدي أقرأ الدفتر، بس مش ملاقي نظارتي!
examples.trans: I want to read the ledger, only I cannot find my glasses!
Just half a glass, please.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (ببلش, بيبلش).

examples.trans: The brass pipe started heating up right away!
The clock tower started chiming twelve.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تاسعة, plural: تاسعين).

examples.trans: We found a ninth brass key in the box.

examples.text: الباب التاسع كان مخفي ورا الحيط.
examples.trans: The ninth door was hidden behind the wall.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: تانية, plural: تانيين).

examples.trans: Room four is on the second floor.
There is a second sheet behind the letter.

meanings.note: Indicates physical location beneath something.

examples.trans: Let us bring it downstairs into the light.
The wide desk is under the window.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بتحرك, بيتحرك).

examples.text: في قطعة معدن تحركت جوا الصندوق!
examples.trans: A piece of metal shifted inside the box!
The car pulled away from the door.

meanings.note: The number 9.

examples.trans: The quietness in the courtyard is nine out of ten!
She came back in just nine minutes!

meanings.note: The standalone form of the number 3.

examples.trans: Three years was a long time.
One, two, three!

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'eight'; short form تمن (taman) before a plural noun (تمن غرف 'eight rooms').

examples.text: عندنا تمن غرف وتمن مفاتيح نحاس.
examples.trans: We have eight rooms and eight brass keys.
He arrives at eight in the evening.

meanings.note: The number 2.

examples.trans: He has two left on the shelf.
Hold the torch, the two of you!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: أجبنة.

examples.trans: Your glasses are pushed up on your forehead!
He wiped the rain off his forehead.

meanings.note: The standard Levantine Arabic word for 'inside' or 'inwards'.

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
The water is flowing inside!

meanings.note: Standard word for a stone or rock, singular form.

examples.trans: Old stone holds warmth.
She stepped onto the stone step outside.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Life is sweet with kind people.
Never in my life have I seen a prettier view.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: حيطان.

examples.trans: We hung the mirror on the wall.
Stone walls keep the coolness in summer.

meanings.note: Standard word for a geographical or digital map.

examples.trans: Look at the folded map inside the box.
We drew a small map of the street.

meanings.note: Used for the material wood or timber.

examples.trans: The wooden ceiling is warm and quiet.
This is a hand-carved wooden train.

meanings.note: Very frequent Jordanian verb: خليني ('let me'), خلينا ('let us'), خليك ('stay!'), خلي ('keep/leave').

examples.trans: Let us open the door together.
Hot bread makes people pleasant!

meanings.note: The number five, used in counting abstractly or before masculine counted nouns.

examples.trans: It is five to twelve.

examples.text: الدكان على بعد خمس دقايق مشي.
examples.trans: The shop is five minutes' walk away.

meanings.note: Spoken Jordanian numeral 'fifteen' before a counted noun (خمستعشر سنة 'fifteen years').

examples.trans: I have not seen it in fifteen years!
The landing is after fifteen steps.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a number, digit, or phone number.

examples.trans: Here is your key, room number four.
Is there a phone number written on the paper?

meanings.note: Numeral 'seven' (عالسبعة 'at seven o'clock').

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
I booked room seven yesterday.

meanings.note: The number 6.

examples.trans: Room six is on the second floor.
I have six lemons in the basket.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: سخانات.

examples.trans: We started the boiler before breakfast.
The boiler room is down in the basement.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بسمع, بيسمع).

examples.trans: Did you hear the gate bell downstairs?
Inside the courtyard we hear the tree leaves.

meanings.note: Everyday word for a year.

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
I have not seen him for three years.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb for 'to see, look, check' (بشوف / شاف).

examples.trans: Look inside the suitcase, Nour!
I will see you tomorrow at breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian interrogative pronoun for 'what'.

examples.trans: What is that sound?
What is written on the sheet, Rami?

meanings.note: Everyday spoken Jordanian noun for 'the morning' (الصبح in the morning, كل صبح every morning).

examples.trans: I drink black coffee every morning.
The morning bread is still hot.

meanings.note: Adjective used for size (small) or age (young), masculine singular.

examples.trans: We found a little wooden train in the bag.
There are two small streets on the left.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: صناديق.

examples.trans: The screwdriver is inside the toolbox.
We moved four boxes out of the hallway.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: طوابق.

examples.trans: Your room is on the second floor on the right.
The building has three storeys.

طلع.gloss: to go up; go out; come out; turn out

meanings.en: to go up; go out; come out; turn out
meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بطلع, بيطلع).

examples.text: لفائف القرفة هلا طلعت من الفرن!
examples.trans: The cinnamon rolls just came out of the oven!
Go up the stairs to the third floor.

meanings.note: Can refer to physical length, height, or duration of time (e.g., all day).

examples.trans: The rain fell all night long.
Breakfast is free all week long.

meanings.note: Arabic expresses age with عمر + possessive suffix: عمره تمانين سنة ('its/his age is eighty years').

examples.trans: The building is eighty years old.
He has lived in this quarter all his life.

meanings.note: Means 'about' (عن الزبدة), 'off / away from' (عن جبيني), and appears in عن جد ('really!') and عن إذنك ('excuse me').

examples.trans: I will carry the suitcase up for you.
I heard your voices about the butter!

meanings.note: A very common preposition used to indicate location, possession, or presence.

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door.
I have a reservation under the name Suad.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun.

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
The shelves are clean with no dust on them.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian word for a room in a house or building.

examples.trans: We have eight comfortable rooms at the guesthouse.
Room four is ready and clean.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بفتح, بيفتح).

examples.trans: The corner shop opens at seven.
Oh, the door finally opened!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun; فتحة قفل means 'keyhole'. Plural: فتحات.

examples.trans: There is a small keyhole on the front.
Air is coming through the window opening.

meanings.note: Used as a preposition or adverb meaning 'above', 'over', or 'upstairs'.

examples.trans: The window is above the old tree.
Let us go upstairs to see the room.

meanings.note: Preposition for 'in' or 'at', and very commonly used to mean 'there is/are' (existential).

examples.trans: There is a small paper tag on the handle.
There is nobody standing in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: قديمة, plural: قدام).

examples.trans: The courtyard has an old jasmine tree.
The old hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بقرأ, بيقرأ).

examples.trans: I want to read the booking ledger.
Did you read the second page clipped underneath?

meanings.note: Used to count items, or mean a portion, slice, or spare part.

examples.trans: Please have a piece of warm bread.

examples.text: خبزت كيكة مع قطع زوايا زيادة.
examples.trans: She baked a cake with extra corner pieces.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: قفال.

examples.trans: The shopkeeper unlocked the padlock in the morning.
We fitted a new brass lock on the closet.

meanings.note: Past tense of 'to be' for 3rd person masculine singular. Widely used as an auxiliary verb.

examples.trans: How was the bus ride?

examples.text: تاني يوم ما رح يكون ممل!
examples.trans: The second day will not be boring!

meanings.note: An everyday item of furniture for sitting.

examples.trans: We placed eight chairs around the tables.
I tightened the screw on the wooden chair.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: كشافات.

examples.trans: Hold the flashlight steady on the pipe joint.
The flashlight beam is bright and clear in the basement.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لحظات.

examples.trans: Wait a moment, let me read the line.
We waited a moment by the gate.

meanings.note: Core word in إلى اللقاء! ('until we meet again / goodbye!') and also 'reunion / meeting'.

examples.trans: Goodbye, have a pleasant trip!

examples.text: كان لقاء دافي بعد غياب طويل.
examples.trans: It was a warm reunion after a long absence.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بلاقي, بيلاقي).

examples.trans: Tell me how to find the hardware shop.

examples.text: لقيت هاد الصندوق الخشب ورا الحيط!
examples.trans: I found this wooden box behind the wall!

meanings.note: Common conjunction used to introduce a time clause, distinct from the question word 'when' (mita).

examples.trans: Smile when the bell rings!
When I get nervous, my sentences turn long.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: لوحات.

examples.text: شوف لوحة المفاتيح الخشب ورا المكتب.
examples.trans: Look at the wooden key board behind the desk.
We wiped the dust off the brass plate.

meanings.note: Definite الليلة means 'tonight', while indefinite ليلة means 'one night / night of'.

examples.trans: I am going to sleep well tonight.
We booked the room for three nights.

meanings.note: Used mostly as a negative particle for verbs ('didn't') or as a relative pronoun/conjunction ('what' or 'that which').

examples.trans: Paper does not lose room names.
Have tea before you head out.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بميل, بيميل).

examples.trans: Listen when I tilt the box slightly!
The afternoon sun slanted into the courtyard.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مخفية, plural: مخفيين).

examples.trans: A hidden door in the cellar is drawn on the map!
The key was hidden inside the box.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مرسومة, plural: مرسومين).

examples.text: في مفتاح دهبي مرسوم فوق الباب.
examples.trans: There is a golden key painted above the door.
The map is drawn by hand.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسح, بيمسح).

examples.trans: Wipe the dust off the brass plate.
We wiped down the tables before breakfast.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بمسك, بيمسك).

examples.trans: Hold this torch steady right here.
Grab the boxes, Tariq!

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: مطوية, plural: مطويين).

examples.trans: We found an old folded map in the box.

examples.text: في ورقة تانية مطوية ورا الإشعار.
examples.trans: There is a second folded sheet behind the notice.

meanings.note: Refers to metallic materials or sometimes one's inner character.

examples.text: سمعنا صوت قطعة معدن جوا العلبة.
examples.trans: We heard a piece of metal inside the box.
Brass is a sturdy, gleaming metal.

meanings.note: Means both a door key and a mechanic's spanner/wrench (مفتاح حديد iron wrench).

examples.trans: Here is the key to room four.
We have eight brass keys on the board.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian feminine noun. Plural: مفصلات.

examples.text: حطيت نقطة زيت على مفصلة الباب.
examples.trans: I put a drop of oil on the door hinge.
The brass hinges of the chest are intact.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian adjective (feminine: ملزقة, plural: ملزقين).

examples.trans: There is a white envelope taped to the handle.
The key was taped underneath the box.

meanings.note: One of the most basic Arabic prepositions indicating origin.

examples.trans: I am Salma from the kitchen.
Breakfast is from seven-thirty to ten.

meanings.note: Used for the metal or objects made of it.

examples.trans: We polished the brass keys in the morning.
The brass pot is old and engraved.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian masculine noun. Plural: نزل.

examples.text: نزل الساحة فيه تمن غرف هادية.
examples.trans: The courtyard guesthouse has eight quiet rooms.
Welcome to our small guesthouse.

meanings.note: Everyday Jordanian verb; spoken present adds the b- prefix (بنزل, بينزل).

examples.trans: Let us bring the suitcase down into the light.
Let me lower my glasses from my forehead!

meanings.note: Singular نظارة means one pair of glasses in Arabic (نظارتي my glasses); dual نظارتين means two pairs of glasses!

examples.trans: I cannot find my glasses on the desk!
He pulled his glasses down off his forehead and laughed.

meanings.note: Everyday demonstrative pronoun for masculine singular objects.

examples.trans: Here we use this big ledger.
This suitcase is very heavy today.

meanings.note: Signature Levantine word for 'now / right now' (pronounced halla' in Amman).

examples.trans: A taxi just stopped at the door now.
We will check the tag right now.

meanings.note: Cardinal number or used as an indefinite pronoun.

examples.trans: Not a single scratch on the cup!
The gate rang with one strong ring.

meanings.note: Very common spatial preposition in Jordanian Arabic.

examples.trans: Look in the mirror behind the desk.
The hardware shop is past the bridge.

meanings.note: Used in negative constructions or as a strong negative emphasis.

examples.trans: Is the window facing the street or the courtyard?
Not a single drop of water on the table!

meanings.note: The standard interrogative adverb for location in the dialect.

examples.trans: Where is the computer, Tariq?
Where should I put the small spoons?

meanings.note: Vocative particle used when addressing someone directly.

examples.trans: Good morning, Tariq!
Oh, how lovely the sun is after the rain!
